paragraphs.en: In his book The Tipping Point, Malcolm Gladwell argues that “social epidemics” are driven in large part by the actions of a tiny minority of special individuals, often called influentials, who are unusually informed, persuasive, or well connected. The idea is intuitively compelling, but it doesn’t explain how ideas actually spread.
paragraphs.zh: 马尔科姆·格拉德威尔在《引爆点》一书中提出，“社会流行现象”在很大程度上是由极少数特殊人物的行为推动的。这些人通常被称为“有影响力者”，他们要么消息格外灵通，要么特别善于说服别人，要么人脉广泛。这个观点直觉上很有吸引力，却没有解释观念实际上是如何传播的。

paragraphs.en: The supposed importance of influentials derives from a plausible-sounding but largely untested theory called the “two-step flow of communication”: Information flows from the media to the influentials and from them to everyone else. Marketers have embraced the two-step flow because it suggests that if they can just find and influence the influentials, those select people will do most of the work for them. The theory also seems to explain the sudden and unexpected popularity of certain looks, brands, or neighborhoods. In many such cases, a cursory search for causes finds that some small group of people was wearing, promoting, or developing whatever it is before anyone else paid attention. Anecdotal evidence of this kind fits nicely with the idea that only certain special people can drive trends.
paragraphs.zh: 人们认定有影响力者很重要，这源于一种听起来可信、却基本未经验证的理论，即“传播的两级流动”：信息先从媒体传向有影响力者，再由他们传向其他所有人。营销人员接受了这种两级传播理论，因为它意味着，只要找到并影响那些有影响力者，这些被选中的人就会替他们完成大部分工作。这一理论似乎还能解释某些造型、品牌或社区为何会突然出人意料地流行起来。在许多这样的案例中，稍作探究就会发现，早在其他人注意到之前，某一小群人就已经在穿戴、推广或开发相关事物。这类轶事性的证据，恰好吻合了只有某些特殊人物才能引领潮流的观点。

paragraphs.en: In their recent work, however, some researchers have come up with the finding that influentials have far less impact on social epidemics than is generally supposed. In fact, they don’t seem to be required at all.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，一些研究人员在最近的研究中发现，有影响力者对社会流行现象的影响远小于通常的想象。事实上，他们似乎根本不是必需的。

paragraphs.en: The researchers’ argument stems from a simple observation about social influence: With the exception of a few celebrities like Oprah Winfrey – whose outsize presence is primarily a function of media, not interpersonal, influence – even the most influential members of a population simply don’t interact with that many others. Yet it is precisely these non-celebrity influentials who, according to the two-step-flow theory, are supposed to drive social epidemics, by influencing their friends and colleagues directly. For a social epidemic to occur, however, each person so affected must then influence his or her own acquaintances, who must in turn influence theirs, and so on; and just how many others pay attention to each of these people has little to do with the initial influential. If people in the network just two degrees removed from the initial influential prove resistant, for example, the cascade of change won’t propagate very far or affect many people.
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员的论点源于对社会影响力的一个简单观察：除了奥普拉·温弗瑞这样为数不多的名人——他们的巨大影响主要来自媒体，而非人际交往——即使一个群体中最有影响力的人，也并不会与那么多人来往。然而，按照两级传播理论，恰恰是这些并非名人的有影响力者，通过直接影响朋友和同事，被认为推动了社会流行现象。可是，要出现社会流行现象，每个受到这样影响的人还必须去影响自己的熟人，而这些熟人又必须去影响各自的熟人，如此延续下去；究竟有多少人关注其中的每一个人，与最初那位有影响力者几乎没有关系。例如，假如社交网络中与最初的有影响力者仅隔两层关系的人不愿接受影响，那么这种连锁变化就不会传播得很远，也不会影响很多人。

paragraphs.en: Building on this basic truth about interpersonal influence, the researchers studied the dynamics of social influence by conducting thousands of computer simulations of populations, manipulating a number of variables relating to people’s ability to influence others and their tendency to be influenced. They found that the principal requirement for what is called “global cascades” – the widespread propagation of influence through networks – is the presence not of a few influentials but, rather, of a critical mass of easily influenced people.
paragraphs.zh: 基于这一关于人际影响的基本事实，研究人员通过对人群进行数千次计算机模拟，并操控若干与人们影响他人的能力及自身易受影响的倾向有关的变量，研究了社会影响的动态过程。他们发现，所谓“全局级联”——即影响力通过网络广泛传播——的首要条件，并不是存在少数有影响力者，而是存在达到临界规模的大批容易受影响的人。
